accounts.name: claimer
docs: Authorises the claim. Never charged for anything, so this may be a
wallet holding exactly zero COOK.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Funds the rent for the claim record. Usually the relayer, which reclaims
it from the sponsor vault in the same transaction.

accounts.name: claim
docs: Creating this account is what makes a second claim impossible.

accounts.name: claimer
docs: Authorises the claim and ends up owning the position. Charged nothing,
so a wallet with zero COOK can do this.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Funds the rent for the claim record and the position.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Funds the rent for the campaign account. May be the relayer, so somebody
with an empty wallet can still ask for help.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Funds the rent. May be the relayer, so an empty wallet can still organise.

accounts.name: pot
docs: Holds contributions. This is the pot that gets paid out.

accounts.name: bond
docs: Holds collateral. Separate from the pot on purpose: collateral belongs to
the member until they default, and must never be payable as a prize.

accounts.name: owner
docs: Owns the position and supplies the deposit itself.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Funds the rent for a first-time position. May be the relayer, so a user
bridging in for the first time is not blocked by rent.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Funds the rent for a first-time donation record.

accounts.name: slot_hashes
docs: the full sysvar is too large to deserialize on-chain.

accounts.name: tail
docs: The member holding the highest seat, moved down into the seat being
vacated. Omitted only when the leaver already holds that seat.
Seats are handed out as `seat = member_count`, so decrementing the count
on the way out without closing the gap would hand the next joiner a seat
number somebody else already holds, and leave the vacated number owned by
nobody. Both are fatal: draws address members by seat, so a duplicate
means one of the two can never receive a pot while still paying into it,
and an orphaned seat stalls the round until the claim window expires.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Funds the compact winner roster. May be the fee-paying relayer.

accounts.name: payer
docs: Funds the rent for a first-time position.

types.name: Campaign
docs: A request for help. Anyone can open one, there is no approval step and no
platform cut, because the person asking is usually the one who can least
afford either.

fields.name: donor_count
docs: Distinct wallets, not gifts. Giving twice does not inflate it.

types.name: Circle
docs: A rotating savings circle.
Every field below is written once at creation and never changed, which is the
reason anybody should be willing to join one: the organiser cannot raise the
contribution or change the collateral policy after money is committed.

fields.name: contribution
docs: Owed by every member, every round.

fields.name: collateral
docs: Fixed reserve posted on joining. New circles require this to cover every
planned contribution; legacy circles may contain a smaller value but are
blocked by CircleSafety until the remaining reserve is repaired.

fields.name: pot_amount
docs: What the pot holds right now. Reset to zero when a turn is collected.

types.name: CircleRoom
docs: Public campaign details and the invite gate for a circle.
Kept in its own PDA so adding room metadata does not invalidate Circle
accounts that were created before campaign rooms existed.

types.name: CircleRoster
docs: Compact eligibility ledger for a circle.
`Circle` predates winner elimination and is already live at its original
size, so changing that account would make every existing circle unreadable.
This companion PDA keeps two 100-seat bitmaps instead: one authoritative
winner set and one migration-progress set for circles that were already
running when the roster was introduced.

types.name: CircleSafety
docs: Solvency guard for a circle.
A protected circle has enough per-member reserve to cover every remaining
contribution. It is deliberately separate from CircleRoster so this safety
upgrade can be added without changing either of the already-live accounts.

fields.name: relayer
docs: Hot wallet that pays transaction fees. Fee payer only. It is never an
authority over any vault in this program.

fields.name: paused
docs: Blocks new deposits. Withdrawals and harvests stay open.

fields.name: bump
docs: No campaign counter here on purpose. This account is already live on
mainnet at its original size, and adding a field would push it past the
space it was allocated. Campaigns are counted by listing them instead.

types.name: Donation
docs: One per wallet per campaign. Its existence is what makes an honest donor
count possible, and it doubles as the public record of who helped.

types.name: EnvelopeClaim
docs: Existence of this account is the proof that a wallet already claimed.
Creating it twice fails at the runtime level, so double claims are
impossible rather than merely checked.

fields.name: into_jar
docs: True when the claim went straight into a jar instead of a wallet.

fields.name: reward_total
docs: Total rewards ever funded into this jar.

fields.name: reward_distributed
docs: Rewards accounted as streamed so far (Proportional only).

fields.name: reward_claimed
docs: Rewards actually paid out.

fields.name: reward_rate
docs: Lamports per second (Proportional only).

fields.name: total_deposited
docs: Principal currently held in the jar vault. This is the TVL figure.

fields.name: acc_reward_per_share
docs: Reward-per-share accumulator, scaled by ACC_PRECISION.

fields.name: entry_count
docs: Entries handed out so far (Lucky only).

types.name: Member
docs: One per wallet per circle. The public ledger everyone in the group can read:
what you posted, what you paid, what you missed, whether you have had a turn.

fields.name: seat
docs: Position in the circle, and what the draw selects.

fields.name: paid_round
docs: Last round this member settled, by paying or by being slashed.

fields.name: active
docs: False once collateral no longer covers this member's remaining
obligations. Protected circles will not advance until this is restored.

fields.name: reward_debt
docs: Accumulator checkpoint, scaled by ACC_PRECISION.

fields.name: pending
docs: Settled but not yet transferred.

fields.name: entry_index
docs: Entry number for Lucky jars. Meaningless unless `has_entry`.

types.name: Sponsor
docs: One per sponsor. Sponsors fund their own users' gas rather than drawing from
a shared pool, so nobody can spend someone else's balance.

constants.name: MAX_FEE_REIMBURSEMENT
docs: Hard cap on what the relayer may reclaim per sponsored transaction.
It covers two things the relayer fronts on a user's behalf: the transaction
fee (10,000 lamports observed on Cookie Chain) and the rent for any account
the instruction opens, which is about 3.3M lamports for a position plus a
claim record. The cap is what bounds the damage if the relayer key leaks:
draining a 2,000 COOK vault would take 400,000 separate transactions.
